children: Chicago soybean futures edged higher on Monday as Chinese imports of US beans fell in August and traders await the upcoming meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later this week. Wheat and corn gained.
* The most-traded soybeans on the Chicago Board of Trade
fell 0.5% to $13.10-1/2 a bushel by 0145 GMT. CBOT wheat
gained 1.8% at $7.27 a bushel, while corn
* Market players await this week's meeting between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, in which Chinese purchases of soybeans and other US agricultural goods will be among trade issues in focus.
* Chinese imports of soybeans from the United States fell 12% in August from a year earlier, official data showed on Sunday.
* China, the world's largest soybean buyer, brought in 12.14 million metric tons in August, down 1.1% from 12.28 million tons a year earlier and up 5.7% from July.
* In the January-August period, soybean imports from the U.S. fell 34% from a year earlier to 10.66 million tons, while shipments from Brazil rose 5% to 55.14 million tons.
* China had also passed the halfway mark toward its 25 million-ton U.S. soybean purchase target for this year, with shipments beginning in September.
* The US Department of Agriculture, under its daily reporting rules, confirmed private sales of 111,000 metric tons of soybeans to China on Friday.

* Oil prices slid on Monday as investors eyed a recovery in shipments from Saudi Arabia despite ongoing attacks by Yemeni Houthis that have escalated tension in the Middle East while the US and Iran remain in a stalemate.
